varieties.name: Deliciosa
varieties.note: The usual one: plain green, large fenestrated leaves once mature.

varieties.name: Borsigiana
varieties.note: Smaller leaves, closer internodes, quicker to climb. Treated the same in every other way.

varieties.name: Albo Variegata
varieties.note: White sectors, unstable: a shoot that reverts to green will outgrow the rest, and an all-white leaf feeds the plant nothing. Slower, and less tolerant of a dark corner.

varieties.name: Thai Constellation
varieties.note: Cream speckling, stable because it is a tissue-culture cultivar. Slower than plain green but far less temperamental than Albo.

varieties.name: Aurea Variegata
varieties.note: Yellow sectors rather than white, and as unstable as Albo.

watering.label: Keep lightly moist, then partly dry

drainage.label: Airy mix that drains freely without drying immediately

young: Too dark even for a juvenile. Leaves stay tiny and the stem reaches badly.
Dim. A young plant makes entire leaves anyway, so watch size and spacing, not splits.
A little short for its age. Growth is slow but the plant is not in trouble.
established: Too dark. An established plant reverts to small entire leaves and reaches for the window.
Dim. It will grow, but new leaves come in solid when they should be splitting.
A little short. Fenestration comes slowly and on fewer leaves.

young: Comfortable for a young plant. Expect size before splits; fenestration waits on age.
Where a juvenile does well. Entire leaves now are its age, not its light.
Generously lit for its age. Strong growth, and it will drink harder for it.
established: Comfortable. Steady growth and new leaves splitting as they should.
Where this kind is happiest. Leaves come regularly, large and well fenestrated.
Generously lit. Strong growth, and it will drink and feed noticeably harder.

young: Burning, and a juvenile burns sooner: thin leaves and little root to keep water up.
Far too much for a young plant. Expect bleaching within a day or two.
Damaging. A plant this young will not grow out of the marks quickly.
established: Burning. Pale yellow blanching between the veins, then dry brown patches.
Too much. Leaves wash out and the thin tissue around the holes dies back first.
Far too much. Direct light at this level marks the leaves permanently.
